children: Keurig Dr Pepper is selling its minority stake in Chobani back to the yogurt maker ahead of the beverage maker's planned split into two public companies.

Keurig Dr Pepper on Tuesday said it will receive $925 million in its deal with Chobani, including $800 million for its stake in the yogurt maker and $125 million for its manufacturing plant and warehouse in Allentown, Pa.

The Frisco, Texas, company said it will use proceeds from the transactions, slated to close by the end of the month, to pare its debt load as it advances the spinoff of its Peet's and Keurig businesses into a pure-play coffee company.

Keurig Dr Pepper said it will continue to distribute the La Colombe brand's ready-to-drink lattes and other Chobani-owned beverage products through its direct-store-delivery network, and that the companies will continue their long-term licensing, manufacturing and distribution agreement for La Colombe-branded K-Cup pods in the U.S. and Canada.
Privately held Chobani said it plans to invest about $1.2 billion over the next five years in the Allentown campus, creating more than 900 jobs.
